title: Don't Look Back in Anger
subtitle: In a better place, or perhaps in the future.

trails.title: Dress Code
trails.description: Remember, the best clothes for a party are the ones that fit in.

content.text:
To everyone on the Space Monitor Project team:
There's a celebration party this Saturday! Don't forget to wear your best clothes!   —Hissabeth

Medicine Pocket has invented a new Picrasma Candy dessert! It has a beautiful circular shape! Everyone is welcome to try it!   —37

Due to a venue conflict, this week's "Nautika Meet-and-Greet" has been moved from Saturday 15:00 - 17:00 to Friday at the same time.   —Ezra

The study On Picrasma as a Coffee Substitute Safe for Human Consumption has been uploaded to the database.   —X

Ms. Windsong is taking me out to buy proper clothes for the party. The office will be empty today from 14:00 to 18:00. Please don't make a wasted trip.   —Kiperina

... I didn't expect it to be so formal. Alright, I will be there on time.   —Name Day

My appointment as director of the LSCC will officially take effect this Saturday.   —Adler

Regarding the Space Monitor Project team's celebration party, just remember to come. The dress code is just another one of Sylvie's flights of fancy.   —Pointer

items.speaker: Z
items.text: This is a very thorough report.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: And knowing where you stand, it's safe to say Laplace won't be facing many more problems for the time being.
She flips through the files and nods.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Our research will continue until we uncover the truth behind the toybox.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: After we establish the Toybox Research Group, I'll be sure to submit more detailed reports of our results. What you have there is far from our final conclusion on the subject.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Or on our collaboration with the Foundation.
Between compromises, this soon-to-be director has learned how to hold his ground.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Anyone who gives a final answer without careful consideration is either a gambler or a cheat.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: I'm glad to see your prudence and rationality as a researcher remain as dependable as ever.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Of course, I'm even happier you've finally decided to be more than just a researcher.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'm sorry, but even now, I still don't fully understand your decision.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I also have one more condition.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Go ahead.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Before my appointment is officially announced, I want to meet with the Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The Foundation's stance is not fully representative of the Timekeeper's, is it?

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Under the framework of our new bill, the Timekeeper and her team do enjoy a greater degree of autonomy.
An answer that is both ambiguous and clever. Such autonomy still falls within the Foundation's legal framework.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Regardless, this isn't a difficult request to fulfill.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Laplace's research findings have made many major contributions to the Timekeeper's operations. Rebuilding trust during this period of turmoil is essential.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You've become quite proficient at all this.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Heh, and I'm just finally starting to get used to it.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Maintaining Laplace's independence, meeting with the Timekeeper ... Is there anything else?
Enigma is quiet for a moment.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Before the Foundation requests the details of any of Laplace's research, they must inform me what it will be used for.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Can you accept this?

items.speaker: Z
items.text: The Foundation has never deliberately concealed anything from Laplace. We've always guaranteed your right to know.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Yes, but the reasons they provide could easily be half-truths—or arrive late.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I don't mean to make your life difficult, but you know better than I the reality of how the Foundation operates.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Judging by your reaction, you can't make that promise. I expected as much.
She neither confirms nor denies it.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I have no other requests.
All those endless meetings finally prove their worth. The strategic concession—a classic among "expert negotiators."
Not meant to get anything specific, but to make a point.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Very good.
She pauses.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: You'll be notified of the official appointment within the week, after which it will be announced to every department. Hopefully, we won't run into any trouble.
She glances around the room.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: You have a lot of paperwork ahead of you.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Why not start with a tidy-up? Some advice from someone with experience: those paper stacks tend to shrink after a little organization.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Resorting to psychological suggestion?

items.speaker: Z
items.text: If it gets the job done.
Madam Z walks to the door, then turns to say goodbye.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: All in all, congratulations to you, Adler, and to Laplace.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: You've secured a positive future for this place.
She leaves. Enigma, standing surrounded by walls of files, sighs.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Enigma stops outside the meeting room door.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Marguerite.
Laplace is a massive institution, and as such, they rarely cross paths. Last time, they'd exchanged only a brief nod.
He takes a moment to study her.
A cold, metallic gleam runs through the center of her dress, like a butterfly emerging from a dark cocoon of torn fabric and flesh.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You ...

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I've seen your research. Not half bad.
She wears an impeccable smile.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Thank you, Mr. Adler.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: And congratulations.
Brief, but sufficient.
He doesn't want his first act as director to be tearing an irreparable rift through Laplace.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Go on in, Mr. Adler. Everyone's waiting.

items.speaker: Crowd
items.text: Happy birthday!
Party poppers go off with a bang. Colorful ribbons rain down over Enigma.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: W-What the hell are you all doing?
None of this is what he'd expected.
It was supposed to be a brief meeting, but the moment he opened the door, control slipped away from him entirely.

items.speaker: X
items.text: It's a celebration, Mr. Enigma. For your birthday! And for your appointment as director, of course!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Today isn't my birthday.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Oh, that doesn't matter. You can celebrate it early.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: The most important thing is today is a day worth celebrating!

items.speaker: Snake I
items.text: Hiss, there's cake! Is that dairy cream, or something plant-based?
Hissabeth pulls another party popper. The sharp smell halts the snake's investigation.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Wait ...

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Our readings have shown higher concentrations of cortisol and adrenaline in the air.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: We've all been under pressure lately. You most of all, Adler. Your index is higher than anyone else's.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: A celebration like this gives everyone a chance to relax, which, in turn, will make them all the more productive with the upcoming workload.
A "thoughtful" theoretical justification for the party, courtesy of Ulrich.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Well, this is a birthday party, isn't it? Make a wish, Enigma! What's that? You want me to make one on your behalf? Well, if you say so.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: I wish, more than anything in the world, for my approval form to pass today! I need to sample the outer material of the toybox.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Denied! Your Picrasma consumption research already jumped the queue, and we need to maintain the structural integrity of the toybox.
Medicine Pocket rolls their eyes and drifts toward the toybox on the table anyway.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hey. Step away from the bo—no ...
This party seems to have given these geniuses an excuse to run wild.
No one cares anymore what the meeting was supposed to be about.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Listen up!
He raises his voice, helpless.
And his brilliant colleagues finally spare him a moment of their attention.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: As you all know, I will be serving as Laplace's director.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Mmhmm?
X gives an approving whistle.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: No kidding! You don't say.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: We were hardly surprised by the decision.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: You'd already been doing the work for quite some time.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: All this goes to prove that, even though you needed some time to adjust, Madam Lucy's judgment was correct.
Though he'd prepared a few words, he now finds himself thinking carefully about how a leader ought to express themselves.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I suppose I've well and truly picked up some useless habits.

items.speaker: X
items.text: And? Anything else you want to say, Director?
He looks around at his colleagues.
Objectively speaking, they are all gifted, yet in wildly different ways.
Subjectively speaking, they are a handful.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: But they all share the same belief—
Science.
He abandons the speech.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: In short, I will do my best.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Until we find someone better suited for the job.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Those who aren't taken by the "Storm"—where do they go when they die?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: A question that remains to be answered.
A black and white grid of a crossword puzzle.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I don't believe in the existence of "gods." Nor in any heaven or hell.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: *sigh* I wish you could give me your answer, Greta.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I wish I could ask you myself.
He rests his finger on the trigger.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: "Bang."

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The age of humans has come to an end.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: But you can continue living.
A fine pistol. A birthday gift.
A "memento."
A beginning.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: In "our" new age.
